title: Every tidycrm write is logged as the user's, including the ones Athena made
body:
## Summary
Every activity row tidycrm writes says `actor: "user"`, whether a person clicked a gate in the sheet or Athena called the tool; the shared table's CHECK already admits `athena`, and no app in the repo ever writes it.

## Description
examples/tidycrm/lib/mutations.ts logs `actor: "user"` at every write (normalize_fields, flag_stale, resolve_company, merge_contacts, delete_contacts, resolve_pair) and examples/tidycrm/app/api/export/route.ts does the same for export. The same server action serves the sheet's buttons (components/blocks/dossier/Gate.tsx) and the WebMCP tools (components/shell/HostCapabilities.tsx), so the action cannot tell which caller it serves, and the provenance strip the demo exists to show cannot answer "what did the agent do?". examples/demo-kit/src/activity/index.ts:18 already has `CHECK (actor IN ('user','athena','system'))` and its header says Athena "is already a first-class actor". Fixed looks like a trusted caller identity that reaches the server action from the tool handler and not from a client-supplied field (a client-supplied actor would let any caller launder a write), stamped by the library. That is a cross-app channel (demo-kit webmcp, every example app), which is why this is a card.

## Flow
- Athena calls `normalize_fields` through HostCapabilities -> `normalizeAction` -> `normalizeFields` -> `logActivity({ actor: "user" })`
- a person presses the same rule in the sheet's gate -> the same row, the same actor
- the activity log shows two identical rows; nothing says which one the agent made

## Expected impact
The operator reading the log after an unattended run can see which writes the agent made and undo exactly those. Could break: an actor that a caller can set is a forgery channel, so the identity has to come from the transport, not the payload.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the activity log names who made each write
Before: 0 of 7 write sites can log anything but "user" (grep: 7 `actor: "user"`, 0 `actor: "athena"` across examples/*)
After: not taken - needs the caller identity carried from the WebMCP handler to the server action
Method: probe - grep over the write sites; no rung above is reachable without the cross-app channel
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: architecture
evidence:
examples/tidycrm/lib/mutations.ts: logActivity({ actor: "user", ... }) at normalizeFields, flagStale, resolveCompany, mergeContacts, deleteContacts, resolvePair
examples/tidycrm/app/api/export/route.ts:9 logActivity(db(), { actor: "user", action: "export", ... })
examples/demo-kit/src/activity/index.ts:18 actor TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (actor IN ('user','athena','system'))
git grep -n 'actor: "athena"' examples -> no match

title: The export tool hard-codes the CSV filename lib/csv.ts already names
body:
## Summary
The `export` tool in components/shell/HostCapabilities.tsx types `tidycrm-${target}.csv` twice beside `exportFilename` in examples/tidycrm/lib/csv.ts, which the route uses for Content-Disposition.

## Description
examples/tidycrm/lib/csv.ts:`exportFilename(segment)` is the one rule for the downloaded file's name, and examples/tidycrm/app/api/export/route.ts uses it in the Content-Disposition header. examples/tidycrm/components/shell/HostCapabilities.tsx (the `export` handler) sets `link.download = \`tidycrm-${target}.csv\`` and returns `file: \`tidycrm-${target}.csv\`` to the agent - two hand-typed copies. lib/csv.ts is pure and client-safe by its own header ("no server imports, so the route and the UI agree on the shape"), so the handler can import it. A rename in csv.ts would leave the agent told a filename the browser did not save. HostCapabilities.tsx belongs to tidycrm-blocks-ui, so this round could not edit it.

## Flow
- import `exportFilename` in HostCapabilities.tsx
- use it for `link.download` and the returned `file`
- add a source guard beside test/tools.test.ts that forbids the literal

## Expected impact
The file the agent reports and the file the browser saves cannot drift apart. Could break: nothing at runtime; the strings are identical today.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one authority for the export's filename
Before: 3 sites spell the name (csv.ts once, HostCapabilities.tsx twice)
After: 1 site, by the same grep
Method: probe - grep for "tidycrm-${" over examples/tidycrm
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: source guard in a tidycrm-blocks-ui test: HostCapabilities.tsx imports exportFilename and contains no `tidycrm-${` literal (fails today on 2 sites)

title: The export summary counts tidies on records that were since deleted
body:
## Summary
`exportSummary` counts every unreverted revision, including those on contacts deleted or merged away afterwards, so "Normalised N fields on M contacts" can name contacts no longer in the list.

## Description
examples/tidycrm/lib/summary.ts `exportSummary` selects `COUNT(DISTINCT contact_id)` and `COUNT(*)` from `revisions WHERE reverted = 0 AND rules <> ?` with no join to `contacts`, so a tidy on a record later deleted still counts. Since 18bdcdf the page says its figures are "across the whole list", which a deleted record is no longer on. Whether a tidy on a now-deleted record is part of "what the cleanup did" is a product call: counting it describes the work done, dropping it describes the list as handed over. Either is defensible, and the page should say which.

## Flow
- normalize_fields on 5 phone-format contacts -> "Normalised 5 fields on 5 contacts"
- delete_contacts on those 5 -> the export page still says 5 contacts were tidied, 0 of them in the list

## Expected impact
The signed-off page's figures match the list it hands over, or say they include removed records. Could break: campaign.test.ts pins the settled-company figures, which would move the same way if the rule is applied to resolve_company's revisions too.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the page's tidy count describes the list it belongs to
Before: walked: 5 tidied then deleted -> counted 5 (the query has no liveness join)
After: 0 with a join on WORKING, or 5 with the sentence saying "including records since removed"
Method: simulation - walked the query against the write paths; the choice between the two Afters is not a measurement
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence:
examples/tidycrm/lib/summary.ts exportSummary:
  SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT contact_id) AS contacts, COUNT(*) AS fields FROM revisions
   WHERE reverted = 0 AND rules <> ?          -- no join to contacts, no liveness predicate

title: globals.css turns on optimizeLegibility for every glyph on an 800-row sheet
body:
## Summary
examples/tidycrm/app/globals.css sets `text-rendering: optimizeLegibility` on `body`, so every figure and label The Blocks draws is shaped with kerning and ligatures, including the narrow-pinned Martian Mono figures that gain nothing from either.

## Description
examples/tidycrm/app/globals.css:`body { text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; }` applies to the whole page. The sheet renders hundreds of tabular figures in Martian Mono (app/page.tsx), where kerning and ligatures change nothing visible, and optimizeLegibility has a long record of slowing text layout on large pages on mobile engines. Whether it costs anything measurable here is a browser question: a layout-time trace of the sheet at L0/L1 with and without the property. Under the overlay's rules this needs a real browser, so it is a card.

## Flow
- record a performance trace of the root page loading and zooming L0 -> L1 with the property
- remove it (or scope it to the Literata note face) and record again
- compare Layout and Recalculate Style totals

## Expected impact
Faster text layout on the zoom transitions if the trace shows it; otherwise the card is rejected with both figures. Could break: Literata headings lose discretionary kerning if the scope is cut too far.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - text layout cost on The Blocks
Before: not taken (no browser in this round)
After: not taken
Method: simulation - the property's reach (every glyph on the page) read from the stylesheet; a trace needs a browser
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence:
examples/tidycrm/app/globals.css: body { ... text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; }
examples/tidycrm/app/page.tsx: Martian_Mono({ axes: ["wdth"], variable: "--font-bk-fig" }) - "every figure is narrow-pinned Martian Mono with tabular numerals"
